title: Subtle docstring drift: optional params added to runReport() and runDetailBandsMode() without JSDoc update
body: In TASK-subreport-detail-rows-D-polish round 1 docs review, found two Critical gaps in engine.ts: runReport() and runDetailBandsMode() both gained a stackRowLimit parameter in Plan C (P3-S3) but their JSDoc @param blocks were never updated. The parameter is meaningful for callers (optional override for stacking-mode row cap). Both crossProductRows() and buildBandChildIndex() were documented correctly — the drift was isolated to the two top-level dispatch functions. Pattern: when adding optional parameters with defaults to already-documented functions, the @param block is easy to forget because the function still works without callers passing the new arg.

title: Systematic JSDoc gap: calcExprs parameter undocumented in all 4 query builders
body: All 4 query builder functions (buildDetailQuery, buildTotalsQuery, buildSubtotalsQuery, buildGroupedQuery) had the same documentation gap: JSDoc documented 3 parameters but the function signature had 4 — the new `calcExprs: Map<string, string>` parameter was undocumented in all four. This is a systematic pattern: whenever a parameter is added to a family of parallel functions, the JSDoc updates need to happen in all of them. The fix was straightforward — added context-specific `@param calcExprs` to each JSDoc block. Typecheck and lint pass clean after the fix.

title: Plan D columnTypeOverrides persistence — documentation analysis
body:
## Analysis Summary

### Files analyzed
1. `SRC/preact/core/state-serializer.ts` — buildPayload() columnTypeOverrides (line 89)
2. `SRC/preact/core/state-hydrator.ts` — hydrateState() columnTypeOverrides block (lines 389-397)
3. `SRC/preact/tests/core/state-serializer-cto.test.ts` — new test file, 4 tests
4. `SRC/preact/tests/core/state-hydrator-cto.test.ts` — new test file, 5 tests
5. `SRC/preact/core/state.ts` — default `columnTypeOverrides: {}` (line 43)
6. `SRC/preact/types.ts` — AppState.columnTypeOverrides with @property JSDoc (lines 141, 202)
7. `artifacts/designs/parts/column-type-aware-where/CONTRACTS.md` — Persistence Layer section (lines 171-190)
8. `artifacts/designs/pending/DD-dd-column-type-aware-where.md` — Phase 6 design spec

### Verification results

1. **Code comments/docstrings** — PASS. Both files follow project conventions. Hydrator has section header `// ── Column type overrides`. Serializer follows the no-inline-comment pattern used by all other fields in the return object. Function-level JSDoc on buildPayload and hydrateState cover the high-level purpose.

2. **CONTRACTS.md** — PASS. Section lines 171-190 accurately describes:
   - Deep-clone serialization with `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))`
   - Empty object `{}` default
   - Position after detailBandMode in both serializer and hydrator
   - Safe backward-compatible default of `{}`
   - No reference validation for unknown tables
   - STATE_VERSION stays at 2, NOT added to RECOGNIZABLE_KEYS

3. **Design doc alignment** — PASS. All 6 checks match:
   - Serializer: `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(state.columnTypeOverrides || {}))` ✅
   - Hydrator: validates non-null object, defaults to `{}` ✅
   - Position after detail band mode ✅
   - No STATE_VERSION bump ✅
   - NOT added to RECOGNIZABLE_KEYS ✅
   - Default in createAppState ✅

4. **Public API / .rcjson format docs** — No user-facing .rcjson schema documentation exists in the project (pre-existing gap across all fields, not specific to this feature). CONTRACTS.md documents the field at the developer contract level. AppState in types.ts has a @property JSDoc.

5. **Test file headers** — PASS. Both new test files have clear, descriptive JSDoc headers covering scope and behavior.

### Verdict: PASS — no actionable documentation gaps specific to Plan D.

title: JSDoc updated but types unchanged — Part A implementation incomplete
body:
In plan TASK-default-selection-conventions-A-types-and-state (Round 1 review), the implementation was NOT actually performed. All 24 plan steps are marked complete, but:
- All 7 type fields still use `| null` in types.ts and result-set.ts (types NOT changed)
- All 5 factory defaults in core/state.ts and result-set.ts still return `null` (defaults NOT changed)
- Only JSDoc comments were updated (6 in types.ts + 1 in result-set.ts) to describe the NEW convention
This creates a dangerous situation where JSDoc says one thing (empty array = nothing) but the code actually uses `null` for the same purpose. The design doc (DD-default-selection-conventions.md) and CONTRACTS.md already document the NEW convention — they are ahead of implementation. Two skill files (state-lifecycle-orientation/SKILL.md) still reference the OLD convention (`Set<string> | null`), which is currently accurate since the types haven't changed.
